title: Truth and Democracy Coalition Launches New Website
description:
Truth and Democracy Coalition Launches Website to Defend Democracy, Counter Propaganda, and Defend the Constitution at https://TruthandDemocracyCoalition.com

Truth and Democracy Coalition Launches Campaign to Bring Americans Together Around Shared Values. Organizer Richard Procida Produces Programs Designed to Cross Ideological, Religious, and Political lines to Undermine False and Divisive Narratives.

WHITTIER, CA, May 25, 2025 -- On May 30, 2025, at 1 pm PDT in person and on May 31st at 10 am online, Richard Procida will present The Truth and Democracy Coalition's new website, programs, and events designed to reach across ideological, religious, and political lines to build the movement to save democracy. The in-person press conference and community meeting will be at the Liberty Community Plaza at 14181 Telegraph Rd, Whittier, CA 90604-2554. Register for the online press conference at https://tinyurl.com/TDCPressConference

Americans are a propagandized people. Political extremism and the widespread dissemination of divisive propaganda have pitted Americans against one another. All sides have been propagandized. Everyone is impacted. Conservatives, liberals, and radicals all consume propaganda.
The Truth and Democracy Coalition is committed to protecting and strengthening democracy in an era of growing division and disinformation. We bring together individuals from all walks of life—Republicans and Democrats, radicals and moderates, Socialists, Liberals, and Conservatives—to uphold and defend the Constitution while strengthening the foundations of democracy. Our mission is to build a broad, diverse, and engaged movement that empowers individuals and communities to stand against authoritarian threats, defend democratic values, and promote truth in public discourse.
Richard Procida, the founder of the Truth and Democracy Coalition, will present the web page, explain the programs, and answer questions. He is available for media interviews and can be contacted at (562) 665-3317 and RichProcida64@Gmail.com

Author and attorney Richard Procida founded the Truth and Democracy Coalition to unite Americans, counter disinformation, defend the Constitution, and fight for democracy. His vision is to bring conservatives, liberals, and radicals together around shared values. Democracy, freedom, and the rule of law, for example, are foundational American values.

As an attorney who studied constitutional law at American University and authored a textbook on foreign comparative constitutional law, he intuitively recognized the looming threat to democracy and freedom posed by the propaganda war. At a time when many were saying that Trump was "just a symptom" of a larger racist system, Mr. Procida began writing and speaking at rallies calling for impeachment and warning Americans about the threat to democracy posed by the Trump Administration. He started a podcast called Democracy Under Fire which later became The Truth and Democracy Podcast, and wrote articles for LAProgressive.com, BuzzFlash.com, and DemCast.com. He held annual events on January 6th to remember the assault on the capital and prevent it from happening again.

Mr. Procida studied social science and communications with a minor in the Study of Women and Men in Society at the University of Southern California. He studied law at American University, Washington College of Law in Washington, D.C. He also co-authored a survey of laws and social attitudes toward sexually explicit materials in various countries and regions of the world (Social Issues in Global Perspective: Pornography, Lexington Books (2003)). He currently leads the Truth and Democracy Coalition.

The Truth and Democracy Coalition is building the movement to save democracy. We fight for democracy, counter divisive propaganda, and defend the constitution.

description:
Democracy isn’t a gift; it’s a responsibility. It’s the promise that every voice matters, that every life is valued. These cuts strip that promise away, leaving us divided and powerless. But we are not powerless. Together, we can demand a government that prioritizes people over profit, that restores funding to our military, workers, healthcare, and schools. Together, we can revive the democracy they’ve tried to bury.
Our military personnel, who sacrifice everything for our safety, are being abandoned. Funding for veteran services, mental health support, and active-duty resources has been slashed, leaving those who serve to fend for themselves. Workers across industries face stagnating wages and vanishing protections as labor budgets are gutted, forcing families into poverty while corporate profits soar. Medical care, a basic human right, is now a luxury—hospitals are underfunded, staff are overworked, and patients are turned away. Education, the cornerstone of an informed democracy, is crumbling; schools lack resources, teachers are underpaid, and students are left behind in overcrowded classrooms.
These cuts aren’t random. They’re a calculated move to weaken us, to silence us, to keep us too desperate to fight back. When our soldiers, workers, healthcare systems, and schools are starved, so too is our democracy. A nation that cannot care for its people is no democracy at all—it’s a hollow shell, ruled by those who profit from our suffering.
We cannot sit idly by, scrolling through outrage on screens while our country decays. Democracy dies in darkness, but it thrives in the streets, in the voices of the united, in the courage of those who show up. We must take our fight offline, where real change is forged. Join us in a nationwide protest to demand an end to these devastating cuts and a return to a government that serves its people.
The United States, once a beacon of democratic ideals, is crumbling under the weight of relentless cuts that gut the very systems we rely on—our military personnel, workers, medical care, and education. These slashes aren't just budget adjustments; they’re a deliberate attack on the backbone of our society, eroding the foundations of a free and fair nation. Democracy, as we know it, is dead—smothered in the shadows of greed, apathy, and unchecked power. But we, the people, can reignite its flame. It’s time to rise, resist, and reclaim what’s ours through unified, offline action.

title: One Community Dialogue: Know Your Rights, Know Your Power

sponsor.name: Louisiana Organization for Refugees and Immigrants

description:
Description:
In a time of uncertainty and fear—when legislation is being used to chip away at our most basic constitutional rights—it’s more important than ever to stay informed, united, and civically engaged.

Join the Louisiana Organization for Refugees and Immigrants (LORI) for our monthly One Community Dialogue series, held every second Friday of the month, where we come together to learn how to safely and effectively be civically engaged and action in our democracy.

We’ll talk about:
• What’s happening at the Louisiana State Capitol and why it matters
• Your rights—what you still have and how to protect them
• The legislative process—how bills become law and how YOU can be part of the conversation
• Step-by-step guidance on showing up, giving testimony, and making your voice heard

You do not need prior experience. These sessions are open, welcoming, and designed to help us all find our role in shaping a better future—especially for immigrant and refugee communities.

Let’s come together as one community, because this is our democracy, and our voices matter.

Dates: Every second Friday of the month
Location: Zoom (link will be sent after you sign up) 
Time: 5:30PM -6:30PM

Environmental Resilience, Sustainable Growth & Climate Action

Florida is on the frontlines of the climate crisis—and our communities are feeling the impact. From worsening flooding and disappearing coastlines to skyrocketing insurance rates and unchecked development, the time for bold, community-driven action is now.

Join us for this follow-up session with the Sierra Club as we dig into the top concerns raised at the May Day of Action and explore how you can take meaningful action to protect our environment, advocate for smart growth, and demand accountability from decision-makers.

🌿 Key topics include:

Flooding, hurricane intensity & climate resilience
Overdevelopment and the need for sustainable infrastructure
Affordable housing and disaster recovery reform
Resource protection and plastic reduction
Public transportation as a climate solution
💡 You’ll leave with concrete advocacy strategies and actions you can take—locally and statewide—to protect what makes Florida home.

title: Hope is Revolutionary: Remembering the Tulsa Massacre
description:
On May 31, 1921, white mobs burned the thriving Black community of Greenwood—known as Black Wall Street—to the ground, killing hundreds and displacing thousands. Over a century later, we gather not just to remember — but to resist.

Join Hope In Action (HIA) for a community event honoring the legacy of the Tulsa Massacre and affirming that hope is revolutionary in the face of historical and ongoing racial violence.

We remember. We organize. We give back.
We will be peacefully protesting while supporting our community through mutual aid.

We will be collecting monetary donations — all going directly to support the NAACP’s local racial justice efforts.

Let’s make memory active. Let’s turn mourning into movement.
Because remembrance without resistance is not enough.

description:
Last month the Palm Beach County Public School Board held an emergency meeting to remove the policies that enabled people of all identities and backgrounds to feel welcome and do their best work. At the same time,  we know that this board and community still believes in these values. 

We understand the pressure that the board was under but we must mobilize to encourage them to revisit their decision. Their policies have always followed the law and the courts are already delaying Title VI policy enforcement.

Every child deserves to feel seen, heard, and supported in the classroom.  The best way to serve a diverse student population is to have diverse, talented educators and professionals serving them. When students feel like they belong, they’re more likely to thrive—academically and personally.

Please join us in advocating for Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Fairness at Palm Beach School Board Meeting Wednesday June 4th at 5:00!

description:
Hui Aloha ‘O Hawaii would like to invite you to a webinar with the Reverend Dr. Allan Boesak 

Saturday June 7, at 8:00 am

Dr. Boesak, author and global human rights activist, is a South African theologian who played a leading role in the anti-apartheid struggle. Dr. Boesak has received numerous awards and accolades for his work. These include the Robert F. Kennedy Human Rights Award, the Martin Luther King Jr. Peace Award, and the King Hintsa Bravery Award from the Royal Xhosa House. He also holds twelve honorary degrees from prestigious institutions such as Yale University and the University of Geneva. Dr. Boesak will be sharing his wisdom on ways we can maintain hope in politically difficult times and challenging us on ways we can respond within our communities and our nation. 

This talk is cosponsored by Hui Aloha ‘O Hawaii Indivisible, Kaua’i’s Justice and Witness Committee, and the HCUCC Justice & Witness Missional Team. This webinar will take place on Zoom and will include a Q & session. Please join us!  All are welcome!

description:
Please join us for this highly rated Resistance Lab 101 training, developed by Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal. 

The Resistance Lab training was developed specifically for this moment, utilizing the tools and frameworks from numerous organizations specializing in nonviolent resistance movements around the country and around the world as well as Congresswoman Jayapal’s organizing background for 20 years prior to Congress. The training explores how democracies fall, how movements around the world have responded, and the tools and tactics available to us to resist. 

The training goals are to help educate people on how to turn anger, fear and frustration into effective, non-violent action. We want to channel people towards current organizing opportunities while also helping to ensure we are strike-ready and street-ready for any large coordinated actions or opportunities that may come as a result of the destruction of our democracy. 

Congresswoman Jayapal recommends this training is be done in-person in our community. Prior attendees loved being in community with others for this training and the breakout sessions are extremely highly valued in their evaluations. This is a great way to channel energy into immediate action, but also to train on the most effective forms of action and provide frameworks to understand how Democratic backsliding happens around the world and what we can do about it.

title: NO KINGS Mankato
description:
Donald Trump thinks his rule is absolute, but in America, we don’t do “kings.” Since the inauguration, the Trump administration and its enablers have operated as though they have a mandate—but they don’t, and never did. They are going to extremes to empower Trump and enrich themselves, while cutting jobs and services for the rest of us. Now, they’re turning Flag Day into a celebration of Trump.

Join us in Mankato Saturday, June 14, from 11-12:30 pm to say:

We are united against kings.

No using OUR tax dollars to pay for HIS party.

They’ve gone too far: This is bigger than political disagreement. They’ve defied our courts, deported American citizens, disappeared people off the streets, and slashed our services—all while orchestrating a massive giveaway to their billionaire allies. Enough is enough. For anyone who thinks he’s gone too far, this movement is for you.

LOGISTICS

We will rally on the sidewalks along two busy side streets in Mankato, Warren St and South Broad St: north on Broad from Warren to Cherry, and 1-2 blocks east and west of Broad on Warren. 

Based on attendance, we will extend the rally in those 3 directions, following the guidance of rally leaders.

Volunteers will assist participants with logistical information and support on rally sidewalks rather than at a central location.

Please use legal, public parking only. Consider arriving by 10:30 to park and find your place. If able, please use parking ramps and walk. Free municipal ramps include Mankato Place, Civic Center, Second Street, and City Center ramps. The last one is the garage along Riverfront Drive between Cherry and Warren streets.

Bring a sign or two, water, cash for emergencies, and weather-appropriate clothing. The nearest bathrooms are a couple of blocks away, so be prepared for that too.

SAFETY

A core principle behind all NO KINGS events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values, and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events. We ask participants to obey traffic and other laws and be mindful of pedestrians using the sidewalks. There will be a police presence at the event but we will rely on our own peacekeepers, volunteers, and you to assist with de-escalation. If asked by leaders or police to disperse, please do so at once.

This event is co-sponsored by Indivisible St. Peter/Greater Mankato and ACLU MN and COPAL MN. Thank you so much for standing with us!
